A '''Barber–Johnson diagram'''{{example needed|date=December 2018}} is a method of presenting hospital statistics combining four different variables in a unique [[Information graphics|graph]], introduced in 1973.<ref>Barber B. and Johnson D., "The Presentation of Acute Hospital In-patient Statistics", ''Hospital and Health Services Review'', 1973</ref> The method constructs a [[Scatter plot|scattergram]] where [[length of stay]], turnover interval, discharges, and deaths per available bed are combined. These four [[Dependent and independent variables|variable]]s have a common relationship between them and their combination in the diagram permitted a new improved way for analyzing [[Business efficiency|efficiency]] and performance of the hospital sector. The most complete reference about how to construct the diagram could be found in Yates.<ref>Yates, John (1982), ''Hospital Beds: A problem for diagnostic and management'', Heinemann Medical Books.
{{ISBN|0-433-37030-0}}</ref> In this book, the appendix explains in detail the way for elaborating this kind of diagram.
